rationale: DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT4, the second R7 mechanism. The empty-name fix covers a name node that is PRESENT and zero-length; this covers a name node that carries a KEYWORD, which is what tree-sitter's recovery produces when IntelliJ context-parameter markup destroys a class header: the real name ends up inside an ERROR node and the constructor keyword arrives as a direct named child typed as a type_identifier, so a first-name-child scan reads the keyword as the name. Measured over the exact population of the construct — every tracked .kt/.kts containing the fixed string `context(`, 2,033 files, all parsed — the pre-fix analyzer published 2 CLASSES named `constructor` for files that declare `Foo`, and with them `exports (file) -> constructor` and `contains constructor -> constructor` rows. The rejection is type-declaration-ONLY because `constructor` is a Kotlin SOFT keyword and `fun constructor()` is legal: the control class at the bottom of the fixture pins that the function IS published, so the rule cannot be widened to functions by a later reader who sees only the first half. Also measured, and stated because it is the same lesson twice: a stride-13 walk of the WHOLE corpus found 0 occurrences of this defect in both the pre-fix and post-fix analyzer, because neither the fixed-string population nor the stride draw is the population that carries the construct — only the targeted one is.
